oneLiner: 横排为周期（电子层数相同），纵列为族（最外层电子数相同）。
oneLinerEn: Rows are periods (same shells); columns are groups (same valence electrons).
detail: 现行表横排为 7 个周期、纵列 18 列。周期数 = 该元素原子核外电子层数；主族（ⅠA–ⅦA 加 0 族）的族序数 = 最外层电子数，也等于最高正价（O、F 除外）。同一族因最外层电子数相同而化学性质相似（如碱金属ⅠA、卤素ⅦA），这是「元素周期律」里“位置反映结构、结构决定性质”的骨架。短周期（1–3）每族只一两种元素、长周期（4–7）里夹着 d 区的过渡元素，镧系锕系被单列在下方以免表格过宽。定位三个数——周期数看电子层、族序数看最外层、原子序数看质子数——就能在「原子结构」与性质之间来回推算。
detailEn: The modern table runs 7 horizontal periods and 18 vertical columns. The period number equals the atom's number of electron shells, and for a main group (IA–VIIA plus group 0) the group number equals the outer-shell count and the highest positive valence, oxygen and fluorine aside. A group shares chemical behaviour because its members have the same outer count — the alkali metals of group 1, the halogens of group 17 — which is the skeleton of the periodic law, where position reflects structure and structure sets properties (see Periodic Law). Short periods 1–3 hold few elements per group, long periods 4–7 fold in the d-block, and the lanthanides and actinides sit in separate rows below to keep the table from widening. Read three numbers — period for shells, group for outer electrons, atomic number for protons — and you can move between atomic structure and properties (see Atomic Structure).

oneLiner: 从左到右原子半径减小、金属性减弱、非金属性增强。
oneLinerEn: Left to right: radius shrinks, metallic character weakens, nonmetals strengthen.
detail: 同周期从左到右，核电荷递增而新增电子填进同一层、屏蔽增加有限，所以有效核电荷增大、原子半径减小（见「原子半径趋势」）。结果是核对最外层电子的引力增强：失电子变难、金属性减弱，得电子变易、非金属性增强，最高价氧化物对应水化物的酸性递增、碱性递减，气态氢化物稳定性递增。第三周期从 Na、Mg、Al 的金属，到 Si 的类金属，再到 P、S、Cl 的非金属，是最完整的递变样本；稀有气体因壳层已满而单列其外。这是「元素周期律」横着读的方向。
detailEn: Across a period the nuclear charge rises while added electrons enter the same shell, so shielding grows little and the effective pull on the outer electrons strengthens — radius shrinks (see Atomic Radius Trend). Losing electrons then gets harder and metallic character weakens, gaining them gets easier and nonmetallic character grows: the hydroxides of the highest oxides turn from basic toward acidic, and the gaseous hydrides become more stable. Period 3 gives the fullest sample, running from the metals sodium, magnesium and aluminium through metalloid silicon to the nonmetals phosphorus, sulfur and chlorine, with the noble gases set apart because their shells are already full. This is the periodic law read left to right (see Periodic Law).

oneLiner: 从上到下原子半径增大、金属性增强、非金属性减弱。
oneLinerEn: Top to bottom: radius grows, metallic character strengthens, nonmetals weaken.
detail: 同主族从上到下，最外层电子数不变而电子层增多、内层屏蔽加厚，所以原子半径增大、核对最外层电子的引力减弱，失电子更容易、金属性增强，得电子更难、非金属性减弱。卤素是纵着读的一条好线：F、Cl 是活泼非金属，Br 次之，I 已显出金属光泽、氢化物 HI 酸性更强而稳定性下降；碱金属则从 Li 到 Cs 与水反应越来越烈。判据口诀“上非下金、右非左金”，两句合起来就是「元素周期律」。它与「同周期递变规律」一横一纵，构成周期表的两条递变主轴。
detailEn: Down a group the outer count stays the same while more shells are added and inner shielding thickens, so the radius grows and the nucleus grips the outer electron less tightly: electrons are lost more easily and metallic character rises, while gaining them becomes harder as nonmetallic character fades. The halogens make a good vertical line — fluorine and chlorine are vigorous nonmetals, bromine less so, and by iodine a metallic lustre appears while the hydride HI turns more acidic yet less stable; the alkali metals likewise react with water ever more violently from lithium to caesium. The rule reads 'up nonmetallic, down metallic' crossed with 'right nonmetallic, left metallic,' and together these are the periodic law (see Periodic Law). Against the across-a-period trend (see Across a Period) these two form the table's axes of variation.

oneLiner: 金属性指失电子能力，非金属性指得电子能力；分界线附近为类金属。
oneLinerEn: Metallic = losing electrons; nonmetallic = gaining; metalloids sit near the divide.
detail: 金属性看失电子的难易、非金属性看得电子的难易，判据有实测对应：金属性可看单质与水或酸置换氢的本领、最高价氢氧化物碱性强弱；非金属性可看与氢化合的难易、气态氢化物稳定性、最高价含氧酸的酸性。左下角（铯、钫）金属性最强，右上角（氟）非金属性最强。沿 B–Si–As–Te–At 的阶梯线两侧是既有金属性又有非金属性的类金属（硅、锗常作半导体）。越靠这条中线，离子键与共价键的过渡越连续，电负性差正是量这根线位置的尺（见「电负性与电离能」）。它是「同周期递变规律」「同主族递变规律」两条方向合成的总效果。
detailEn: Metallic character is how readily an atom gives up electrons and nonmetallic how readily it takes them, and both have hands-on tests: gauge metallic strength by how a substance frees hydrogen from water or acid and by how basic its highest hydroxide is, and gauge nonmetallic strength by how easily it joins hydrogen, how stable that hydride is, and how strong its highest oxyacid. The lower-left (caesium, francium) is most metallic and the upper-right (fluorine) most nonmetallic. Along the stepped boron–silicon–arsenic–tellurium–astatine line sit the metalloids, both metallic and nonmetallic, with silicon and germanium used as semiconductors. Nearer the divide, ionic-to-covalent bonding shades over continuously, and the electronegativity gap is the ruler measuring position on it (see Electronegativity & Ionization). This is the combined effect of the two directions, across a period and down a group.

oneLiner: 同周期减小、同主族增大；稀有气体因计量方式通常单独较大。
oneLinerEn: Shrinks across a period, grows down a group; noble-gas values differ by convention.
detail: 原子半径不是实测的硬边，而是把相邻原子核间距取一半推出来的，所以比较时必须守住同一套口径。规律只有两句：同周期从左到右逐渐减小，同主族从上到下逐渐增大。前者是因为电子都填进同一层、屏蔽几乎不增，而核电荷一步步加大，外层被拉得更紧；后者是因为每往下就多出整整一个电子层，层数的作用压过了核电荷的增加。两个常考的比较：一、比微粒半径先看电子层数，层多则大；层数相同再看核电荷，核大则小（O²⁻、F⁻、Na⁺、Mg²⁺、Al³⁺ 都是 2、8 结构，只差质子数，所以依次缩小）。二、同种元素的原子与离子，阳离子一定小于原子（少了一层），阴离子一定大于原子（层没变而电子间斥力变大），所以 Na⁺ 小于 Na、Cl⁻ 大于 Cl。稀有气体要单独说明：它的半径是范德华半径，与相邻元素的金属或共价半径不是同一口径，因此画在同一张折线图上常常突然变大，中学阶段一般不参与比较。
detailEn: An atomic radius is not a measured hard edge: it comes from halving the distance between neighbouring nuclei, so every comparison has to stay inside one convention. The rule is two sentences — radii shrink across a period and grow down a group. In the first case the electrons go into the same shell and screening barely rises while the nuclear charge does, so the outer electrons are pulled tighter; in the second a whole new shell is added, and shell count beats nuclear charge. Two comparisons are examined every year. Particles with different shell counts are ranked by shells first, and where the shell structure is identical the larger nuclear charge wins — O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺, Mg²⁺, Al³⁺ are all 2,8 and shrink in that order. For one element the cation is always smaller than the atom (a shell gone) while the anion is larger (same shell, more electron repulsion), so Na⁺ is under Na and Cl⁻ over Cl. Note the convention clash for noble gases: their figure is a van der Waals radius, not a metallic or covalent one, which is why they jump at the end of a plot and why the school course leaves them out of the ranking.

oneLiner: 电负性衡量吸引共用电子能力（氟最大）；电离能是失电子所需能量。
oneLinerEn: Electronegativity gauges electron attraction (F largest); ionization energy is to remove an electron.
detail: 电负性是原子在「共价键」里抢共用电子对的能力，鲍林标度里氟最大（4.0）、向左下递减；两原子电负性差越大，键越偏向离子性（一般差到 1.7 及以上判离子键为主）。电离能是从气态原子移走一个电子所需的能量，第一电离能同周期左低右高、同主族上高下低；当要拆的是已排满的稳定壳层或半满轨道时，会出现反常台阶（如 Be、N、稀有气体比相邻元素偏高）。两者都随核电荷增大而升高、随半径增大而降低，本质是同一份引力的两面——一个说抢电子、一个说甩电子。同一道电负性差，还能解释为什么 NaCl 是离子化合物而 HCl 是共价分子。
detailEn: Electronegativity is how hard an atom pulls a shared pair in a covalent bond (see Covalent Bond); on the Pauling scale fluorine is highest at 4.0 and the value falls toward the lower left, and the bigger the gap between two atoms the more the bond leans ionic, with a gap near 1.7 and above taken as mainly ionic. Ionization energy is the energy needed to strip one electron from a gaseous atom; the first ionization energy rises left to right across a period and falls down a group, with sudden steps where a full shell or a half-filled subshell must be broken, as in beryllium, nitrogen and the noble gases. Both climb with nuclear charge and fall with radius, being two faces of one grip — one word about seizing electrons, the other about letting them go. The same gap explains why sodium chloride is an ionic solid while hydrogen chloride is a covalent molecule.

oneLiner: 周期表中部 d 区元素，多为有色、可变价、易形成配合物。
oneLinerEn: Central d-block elements: often colored, multiple valences, complex-forming.
detail: 过渡元素是周期表中部填 d（或 f）轨道的一区，价电子除最外层还动用次外层 d 电子，所以常有多价态（Fe 有 +2、+3，Mn 从 +2 到 +7），不像主族多只一个价。多数有颜色、易形成配合物，因为空的 d 轨道能接受孤对电子；水合离子与许多化合物显色正源于 d 电子跃迁吸收可见光。它们熔点高、密度大、硬度高，是结构与功能材料的主力：Fe 造钢、Cu 导电、Ti 轻质耐蚀，催化剂更是遍地（Fe 合成氨、V₂O₅ 接触法制硫酸、Pt 与 Pd 净化汽车尾气）。同一周期内相邻过渡金属半径变化很小，这正是「同周期递变规律」到 d 区放缓的地方。
detailEn: Transition elements are the central block that fills d or f orbitals; their valence reaches into the inner d shell as well as the outer one, so they show many oxidation states — iron at +2 and +3, manganese from +2 up to +7 — unlike main-group atoms that usually sit at one. Most are coloured and form complexes readily, since empty d orbitals can accept lone pairs, and the hues of their hydrated ions come from d electrons absorbing visible light. They are hard, dense and high-melting workhorse materials: iron into steel, copper conducting wires, titanium light and corrosion-proof, and catalysts everywhere (iron for ammonia, vanadium pentoxide for sulfuric acid, platinum and palladium in exhaust cleanup). Radii barely change between neighbours within a period, which is where the across-a-period trend flattens out in the d block (see Across a Period).

oneLiner: 最外层电子已满，化学性质极稳定，过去称惰性气体。
oneLinerEn: Filled outer shells make them extremely stable, once called inert gases.
detail: 氦、氖、氩、氪、氙、氡的最外层已排满（氦 2 个、其余 8 个稳定结构），电离能极高、几乎不得失也不共用电子，故化学性质极不活泼，旧称惰性气体。氖、氩多做保护气与霓虹灯，氦用于低温、超导与气球（密度小又不可燃，比氢气安全），氙可做高压灯与麻醉。说“惰性”只是相对的——1962 年巴特利特制出第一例稳定的含氙化合物，较重、半径较大的氙、氪外层电子离核远、易被强氧化剂拽走而能成键。它们正是「同周期递变规律」里每个周期收尾的那一列，壳层填满处递变到此归零。
detailEn: In helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon the outer shell is already full (two for helium, eight for the rest), ionization energies are very high, and the atoms neither give, take nor share electrons readily, which is why they were long called inert gases. Neon and argon serve as shield gases and in signs, helium in cryogenics, superconductors and balloons (light and non-flammable, safer than hydrogen), and xenon in powerful lamps and anaesthesia. Inert is only relative: in 1962 Bartlett made the first stable xenon compound, and the heavier, larger atoms such as xenon and krypton hold their outer electrons far enough from the nucleus that strong oxidizers can wrest them into bonds. They are the closing column of every period, where the across-a-period trend ends at a full shell (see Across a Period).
